## How the score was worked out

Each result implies a score on its own, after adjusting for how hard that test is and who ran it. The model's score is their weighted average, with a small pull toward the middle for thinly tested models. Each test's weight is its *counts* column above; here it is added up by who ran the tests. ## How to run it

### llama.cpp (recommended)

1. Install llama.cpp. Homebrew and winget installs name the commands llama-cli and llama-server instead. [Other ways to install](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/install.md)
   
   ```sh
   # macOS / Linux
   curl -LsSf https://llama.app/install.sh | sh
   # Windows
   irm https://llama.app/install.ps1 | iex
   ```

2. Run Yi 34B 200K (base) (Q4_K_M, needs ~20.7 GB, from [huggingface.co/TheBloke](https://huggingface.co/TheBloke/Yi-34B-200K-GGUF/tree/0e5be0d99e4f9636c795d4bd11bbf7ee3b452536))
   
   ```sh
   llama cli -hf TheBloke/Yi-34B-200K-GGUF:Q4_K_M
   ```

3. Or start a local server and open the address it prints (http://localhost:9931)
   
   ```sh
   llama serve -hf TheBloke/Yi-34B-200K-GGUF:Q4_K_M
   ```

Other versions: Q8_0 (~36.5 GB) `llama cli -hf TheBloke/Yi-34B-200K-GGUF:Q8_0`

### LM Studio

1. Install LM Studio. Open the app once before using the lms command. [Download it (macOS / Windows / Linux)](https://lmstudio.ai/download)

2. Run Yi 34B 200K (base) (Q4_K_M, needs ~20.7 GB, from [huggingface.co/TheBloke](https://huggingface.co/TheBloke/Yi-34B-200K-GGUF/tree/0e5be0d99e4f9636c795d4bd11bbf7ee3b452536))
   
   ```sh
   lms get https://huggingface.co/TheBloke/Yi-34B-200K-GGUF@Q4_K_M -y
   ```

3. Then run lms ls to see its name, and lms chat followed by that name

Other versions: Q8_0 (~36.5 GB) `lms get https://huggingface.co/TheBloke/Yi-34B-200K-GGUF@Q8_0 -y` · 8bit (~36.5 GB, Mac only) `lms get https://huggingface.co/Fmuaddib/Yi-34B-200K-mlx-8Bit -y`

### Ollama

1. Install Ollama. [Download it (macOS / Windows)](https://ollama.com/download)
   
   ```sh
   # Linux
   curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh
   ```

2. Run Yi 34B 200K (base) (Q4_K_M, needs ~20.7 GB, from [huggingface.co/TheBloke](https://huggingface.co/TheBloke/Yi-34B-200K-GGUF/tree/0e5be0d99e4f9636c795d4bd11bbf7ee3b452536))
   
   ```sh
   ollama run hf.co/TheBloke/Yi-34B-200K-GGUF:Q4_K_M
   ```

Other versions: Q8_0 (~36.5 GB) `ollama run hf.co/TheBloke/Yi-34B-200K-GGUF:Q8_0`

### MLX (Mac)

1. Install MLX (Mac). Apple silicon Macs only, text only.
   
   ```sh
   # with uv
   uv tool install mlx-lm
   # or
   pip install mlx-lm
   ```

2. Run Yi 34B 200K (base) (8bit, needs ~36.5 GB, Mac only, from [huggingface.co/Fmuaddib](https://huggingface.co/Fmuaddib/Yi-34B-200K-mlx-8Bit/tree/5480038b2192c6972fbd48be1d6868a2400db4c6))
   
   ```sh
   mlx_lm.chat --model Fmuaddib/Yi-34B-200K-mlx-8Bit
   ```

3. Or start an OpenAI-compatible server at http://localhost:8080/v1
   
   ```sh
   mlx_lm.server --model Fmuaddib/Yi-34B-200K-mlx-8Bit
   ```

### Other ways to run it

1. Run it as published (BF16, needs ~68.78 GB, from [huggingface.co/01-ai](https://huggingface.co/01-ai/Yi-34B-200K/tree/e0ae1afac6b69f604556efd441ab4befafb2a835))
   
   ```sh
   uv run --with torch --with 'transformers<5' --with accelerate python -c "from transformers import pipeline; print(pipeline('text-generation', model='01-ai/Yi-34B-200K', torch_dtype='auto', device_map='auto')('Once upon a time', max_new_tokens=40)[0]['generated_text'])"
   ```

Official weights and documentation: [huggingface.co/01-ai](https://huggingface.co/01-ai/Yi-34B-200K)
